hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Across four HEK293 wells per genotype, APOE4-expressing cells had higher baseline LC3II/LC3I and LC3 abundance than APOE3-expressing cells. These measures alone leave the direction of autophagic flux unresolved.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4–mCh cells had a significantly higher LC3II/LC3I ratio and significantly higher LC3 abundance (Fig. 1A). An increase in the LC3II/LC3I ratio may suggest either high macroautophagic flux, a late stage block of autophagy at the level of the lysosome causing autophagosome accumulation, or both.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher baseline LC3II/LC3I ratio and LC3 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 embryonic kidney cells, ATCC CRL-1573; one selected stable clone per APOE–mCherry isoform; basal nutrient-rich culture; western blotting; no human brain cells or lipid-mediated mechanism tested.
rows.Data location: Fig. 1A; intracellular APOE comparison additionally stated in Results under lysosomal isoform-specific degradation

rows.Finding description: Across three HEK293 wells per isoform, APOE4-expressing cells had larger individual LAMP1-positive lysosomal surfaces than APOE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: Imaris analysis revealed that APOE4–mCh cells had significantly higher colocalization between APOE and lysosomes, and significantly greater average surface area of individual lysosomal and APOE puncta (Fig. 3A) than did APOE3–mCh cells, suggesting greater trafficking to lysosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (larger LAMP1-positive lysosomal compartments)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 stable APOE3–mCherry versus APOE4–mCherry cells; CellLight LAMP1–GFP; live confocal microscopy; average individual lysosomal surface area measured with Imaris.

rows.Finding description: After 24 hours of conditioned-medium exposure in three ST14A wells per isoform, APOE4 preferentially colocalized with late rather than early endosomes, whereas APOE3 showed no such preference.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 colocalized with late endosomes significantly more than with early endosomes, whereas APOE3 did not.
rows.Finding summary: Rab7 versus EEA1 colocalization was significantly greater within APOE4-treated cells. APOE3-treated cells showed no significant preference. An isoform-by-marker interaction was not reported.
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized rat neuron-like ST14A cells; APOE3–mCherry or APOE4–mCherry conditioned medium for 24 h; fixed-cell mCherry, EEA1 and Rab7 immunostaining; confocal microscopy and Imaris analysis.

rows.Finding description: Across four HEK293 wells per genotype, APOE4-expressing cells had higher Beclin1 and lower ATG7 protein abundance than APOE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: Relative to APOE3–mCh cells, APOE4–mCh cells had increased Beclin1 protein, suggesting upregulation of macroautophagy, but ATG7 levels were significantly lower (Fig. 1C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher Beclin1 and lower ATG7 protein abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 cells, ATCC CRL-1573; stable APOE3–mCherry versus APOE4–mCherry clones; basal culture; western blotting of autophagy proteins.
rows.Data location: Fig. 1C; LAMP2A comparison in final paragraph of the first Results subsection

rows.Finding description: Across three HEK293 wells per isoform, APOE4 showed greater colocalization with LAMP1-positive lysosomes than APOE3.
rows.Finding quote: Imaris analysis revealed that APOE4–mCh cells had significantly higher colocalization between APOE and lysosomes, and significantly greater average surface area of individual lysosomal and APOE puncta (Fig. 3A) than did APOE3–mCh cells, suggesting greater trafficking to lysosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater APOE–LAMP1 colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 stable APOE3–mCherry versus APOE4–mCherry cells; transduced CellLight LAMP1–GFP; live confocal imaging and Imaris analysis; three images per well.

rows.Finding description: Across three HEK293 wells per isoform, dual-tagged APOE4 had a lower green/red fluorescence ratio than APOE3, indicating greater acidic-compartment localization without measuring a lysosomal pH difference.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4–mCh–SepH cells had a significantly lower ratio of green to red fluorescence compared with APOE3–mCh–SepH cells, indicating a greater degree of lysosomal localization of the protein (Fig. 3B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower green/red APOE fluorescence ratio and greater acidic-compartment localization)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 cells stably expressing APOE3–mCherry–SepHluorin or APOE4–mCherry–SepHluorin; live confocal imaging; pH-sensitive green versus pH-resistant red fluorescence; three images per well.

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 reduced prohibitin abundance to 0.692x, consistent with reduced mitophagy-associated lysosomal cargo.
rows.Finding quote: This suggests that the depletion of prohibitin from the LysoIP eluate in APOE4 relative to APOE3-treated cells is specific to the lysosome-enriched fraction, and does not reflect overall reduced abundance.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (lower lysosomal prohibitin abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatic TMEM192–HA cells with endogenous APOE3; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in legends versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Table S1, accession P35232; Fig. 7D and Fig. S7C

rows.Finding description: Within APOE4-expressing HEK293 cells, rapamycin caused no significant change in LC3 abundance across three wells per treatment, whereas abundance increased in APOE3 and control cells.
rows.Finding quote: However, LC3 abundance was increased with Rap only in APOE3–mCh and mCherry cells, with no change in APOE4–mCh cells.
rows.Finding summary: (rapamycin) -> (LC3 abundance increased in APOE3 and mCherry controls, with no change reported in APOE4)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293 stable APOE4–mCherry cells, with APOE3–mCherry and mCherry controls; 10 nM rapamycin for 4 h; western blotting; treatment response rather than direct genotype perturbation.

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 reduced NDUFB4 abundance to 0.258x, consistent with reduced lysosomal mitochondrial-cargo delivery.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (lower lysosomal NDUFB4 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatic TMEM192–HA cells with endogenous APOE3; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in legends versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Table S1, accession O95168; underlying experiment Fig. S7C

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 reduced NDUFV2 abundance to 0.657x, consistent with reduced lysosomal mitochondrial-cargo representation.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (lower lysosomal NDUFV2 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatic TMEM192–HA cells with endogenous APOE3; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in legends versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Table S1, accession E7EPT4; underlying experiment Fig. S7C

rows.Finding description: APOE4 versus APOE3 increased lysosomal representation of secretory/endocytic cargo in four HepG2 samples per group, which the authors interpreted as enhanced trafficking/degradation of those cargoes.
rows.Finding quote: Proteins enriched in the lysosome of APOE4-containing cells included a variety of secretory and endocytosis pathway proteins, including several resident Golgi proteins, membrane-tethering proteins and extracellular matrix proteins (Fig. 7D; Fig. S7D, Table S1). Thus, APOE4 appears to inhibit the lysosomal trafficking of mitochondria while enhancing the lysosomal degradation of secretory or endocytic vesicles.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (greater lysosomal representation of secretory/endocytic cargo)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 cells with endogenous APOE3 and stable TMEM192–HA; APOE–mCherry conditioned-medium exposure; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in Results/legend versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 altered multiple lysosomal protein abundances, including changes not reproduced in the same direction by mCherry control medium.
rows.Finding quote: We identified proteins that were uniquely altered in APOE4-treated cells relative to APOE3-treated cells, and were not significantly altered between mCh- and APOE3-treated cells in the same direction (Fig. S7C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (altered lysosomal proteomic composition)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 cells with endogenous APOE3 and stable TMEM192–HA; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in supplementary legend versus 48 h followed by 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Fig. S7C; numerical comparisons in Table S1

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 reduced METTL15 abundance to 0.098x, contributing to the mitochondrial-cargo depletion pattern.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (lower lysosomal METTL15 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatic TMEM192–HA cells with endogenous APOE3; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in legends versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Table S1, accession A6NJ78; underlying experiment Fig. S7C

rows.Finding description: In four HepG2 lysosomal samples per group, APOE4 versus APOE3 reduced FAHD1 abundance to 0.418x, contributing to the mitochondrial-cargo depletion pattern.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 medium -> APOE4 medium) -> (lower lysosomal FAHD1 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatic TMEM192–HA cells with endogenous APOE3; APOE–mCherry conditioned medium; LysoIP and label-free LC–MS/MS; 24 h in legends versus 48 h plus 4 h bafilomycin in Methods.
rows.Data location: Table S1, accession Q6P587; underlying experiment Fig. S7C

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Following a three-hour myelin pulse, E4 microglia exhibited a significantly longer half-life of intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia, suggesting slower degradation of internalized myelin.
rows.Finding quote: We also observe a significantly longer half-life of red fluorescence decay in E4 microglia relative to E3, WT and KO microglia, which were not significantly different from one another (Figure S4b, see Methods). This suggests that in addition to exhibiting increased phagocytic uptake, E4 microglia may exhibit impaired ability to degrade internalized myelin.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (longer internalized-myelin fluorescence half-life, suggesting impaired degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour pulse of 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red myelin followed by washout and hourly IncuCyte imaging for six days; phase-confluence-normalized fluorescence fitted with a one-phase exponential decay model using the six-hour fluorescence value as Y0; half-life calculated as ln(2)/K.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S4B, E4 versus E3

rows.Finding description: Following myelin challenge, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes whereas E4 microglia showed no significant further acidification and a nonsignificant pH increase, without a reported genotype-by-treatment interaction test.
rows.Finding quote: Following treatment with myelin, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes (Figure S3). Interestingly, a similar decrease in lysosomal pH was observed in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia at baseline. As lysosome function is optimal at lower pH, these effects may reflect activation of the lysosomal degradation machinery to cope with the increased burden of internalized debris following myelin challenge in E3 microglia, or in E4 vs E3 microglia even before myelin challenge. E4 microglia did not exhibit further acidification following myelin challenge but rather a slight (albeit not significant) increase of their lysosomal pH (Figure S3).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no significant further lysosomal acidification after myelin challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; untreated cells compared with cells exposed to myelin for three hours and assessed at 24 hours; lysosomal pH measured using LysoSensor and flow cytometry.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S3; baseline-to-myelin pH responses, exact panels unavailable

rows.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 and E3 microglia showed no significant difference in neutral-lipid colocalization with late-endosomal RAB7 across four independent experiments per group.
rows.Finding quote: Low levels of colocalization between BODIPY and RAB7 were observed and no statistically significant difference across genotypes could be inferred (Fig. 3e), suggesting a portion of neutral lipids accumulated in early endosomes or other RAB5-positive organelles rather than RAB7-positive organelles.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in neutral-lipid colocalization with late-endosomal RAB7)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge and analysis at 24 hours; BODIPY neutral-lipid staining and RAB7 immunofluorescence colocalization assessed using Pearson correlation, Fisher transformation, and a two-sample z-test.

rows.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had significantly more acidic lysosomes than E3 microglia, opposing a simple APOE4-associated failure of lysosomal acidification.
rows.Finding quote: We then further used LysoSensor dye to measure the pH of lysosomes, which were significantly more acidic in E4 microglia when compared to E3 microglia (Figure S3).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal pH at baseline)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; untreated baseline cells assessed using 2 μM LysoSensor Green DND-189 for 10 minutes and live-cell flow cytometry, with an intracellular pH calibration procedure described in Methods.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S3; baseline E4-versus-E3 pH comparison, exact panel unavailable

rows.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 microglia had greater LysoTracker fluorescence than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, interpreted as increased lysosomal mass.
rows.Finding quote: E4 microglia again exhibited increased lysosomal mass relative to E3 microglia as measured by both Lyso-Tracker gMFI via flow cytometry (Fig. 3f) and CD68 immunostaining integrated density via fluorescence microscopy (Fig. 3g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher LysoTracker-estimated lysosomal mass after myelin challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; LysoTracker Red DND-99 staining and live-cell flow cytometry at 24 hours.

rows.Finding description: At 72 hours after myelin application, E4 microglia retained higher intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia across three to five independent experiments, consistent with greater cargo persistence but confounded by greater initial uptake.
rows.Finding quote: Post-hoc t-tests at select time points identified significant differences (FDR adj. p-value = q < 0.05) between E4 microglia and microglia of other genotypes as early as 3 hours (E4 vs E3: q = 2.2 × 10−06, d = 3.7 CI95% [0.7, 6.6]; E4 vs KO: q = 1.1 × 10−06, d = 2.2 CI95% [0.3, 4.0], E4 vs WT, q = 2.6 × 10−06, d = 3.9 CI95% [1.1, 6.6]) and up to 72 hours (E4 vs E3: q = 0.001, d = 4.7 CI95% [1.7, 7.6], E4 vs KO, q = 0.1, d = 2.3 CI95% [0.4, 4.1], E4 vs WT, q = 0.03, d = 4.6 CI95% [1.4, 7.7]) post-treatment.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher persistent intracellular myelin fluorescence at 72 hours)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; three-hour pulse of 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red myelin followed by washout; normalized IncuCyte fluorescence measured 72 hours after initial application.
rows.Data location: Fig. 2C, E4 versus E3 at 72 hours

rows.Finding description: At 24 hours after myelin application, E4 microglia had higher late-endosomal RAB7 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group.
rows.Finding quote: E4 microglia again displayed higher levels of both RAB5 and RAB7 relative to E3 microglia (Fig. 3c, d).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher late-endosomal RAB7 abundance after myelin challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; RAB7 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell measured 24 hours after initial application.

rows.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 microglia had higher CD68 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, providing a surrogate for increased lysosomal mass.
rows.Finding quote: E4 microglia again exhibited increased lysosomal mass relative to E3 microglia as measured by both Lyso-Tracker gMFI via flow cytometry (Fig. 3f) and CD68 immunostaining integrated density via fluorescence microscopy (Fig. 3g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosome-associated CD68 abundance after myelin challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; CD68 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell at 24 hours.

rows.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had higher RAB7 immunostaining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, indicating greater late-endosomal marker abundance without establishing impaired function.
rows.Finding quote: In addition, the levels of both early endosome (RAB5) and late endosome (RAB7) markers were increased in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia (Fig. 1e), which may be reflective of an increased number and/or size of endosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher late-endosomal RAB7 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia isolated from pooled forebrains of P1–3 human APOE3 or APOE4 homozygous targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; enriched after approximately 28 days in mixed glial culture, replated and allowed to adhere overnight; baseline RAB7 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell. These are mouse cells expressing human APOE, not human brain cells.

rows.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had higher CD68 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, providing another surrogate for increased lysosomal mass.
rows.Finding quote: In addition, integrated density of fluorescent immunostaining of the lysosome-associated protein CD68 was increased in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia, further demonstrating an increase in lysosomal mass (Fig. 1g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosome-associated CD68 abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately 28-day mixed glial culture followed by enrichment and overnight adhesion; untreated cells assessed by CD68 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell.

rows.Finding description: Following a three-hour myelin pulse, E4 microglia showed higher intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia during six-day monitoring across three to five independent experiments, a composite readout of uptake, acidification, and cargo persistence.
rows.Finding quote: E4 microglia exhibited significantly higher integrated intensity of red fluorescence relative to E3 microglia as well as microglia from mice homozygous for the WT or KO allele of mouse Apoe (Fig. 2b).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher intracellular acid-sensitive myelin fluorescence over time)
rows.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; enriched after approximately four weeks in culture; exposed to 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red-labeled wild-type mouse myelin for three hours, washed, and imaged hourly for six days using IncuCyte; fluorescence normalized to phase confluence.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: After rapamycin, APOE4 microglia displayed less tandem-LC3 reporter conversion to red-only puncta than APOE3 microglia, interpreted as impaired autophagosome delivery to lysosomes.
rows.Finding quote: Thus, autophagosomes delivery to lysosomes is hampered in APOE4 microglia.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less autophagosome delivery to lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4 and transiently transfected with tandem LC3-EGFP-mRFP; 48 h after transfection, 150 nM rapamycin for 24 h; confocal microscopy of yellow and red-only puncta. No lipid-metabolism assay.

rows.Finding description: Following rapamycin, the reported red-only LC3 fraction was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia, 13.84% ± 1.96 versus 41.03% ± 3.268, with at least 50 cells per treatment analyzed.
rows.Finding quote: We found that following rapamycin treatment, 41.03% ± 3.268 of autophagosomes were fused with the lysosomes (RFP-tagged red puncta), compared to 13.84% ± 1.96 in the APOE4 expressing microglia (Fig. 6).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower red-only LC3 fraction indicating reduced autolysosome formation)
rows.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; transient tandem LC3-EGFP-mRFP reporter; 150 nM rapamycin for 24 h beginning 48 h after transfection; confocal imaging and puncta-area quantification. Acid-sensitive reporter behavior supports a flux/lysosomal-delivery interpretation but does not isolate fusion from acidification.

rows.Finding description: Following chloroquine treatment, normalized p62 was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia, 0.629 ± 0.068 versus 0.954 ± 0.059, supporting reduced autophagic flux. Effect is the ratio of the two group values printed in the quote (0.954 ± 0.059 and 0.629 ± 0.068).
rows.Finding quote: However, the levels of p62 following chloroquine treatment were significantly higher in APOE3 microglia compared to APOE4 microglia (0.954 ± 0.059 and 0.629 ± 0.068, respectively).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower p62 accumulation during lysosomal blockade)
rows.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; experiment used 1 h EBSS with or without 10 µM chloroquine; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to APOE3 control. The numerical CQ comparison is not unambiguously assigned to CQ alone versus EBSS plus CQ in the supplied narrative.

rows.Finding description: After 0.5 h starvation, normalized p62 remained higher in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia: 0.932 ± 0.065 versus 0.592 ± 0.012.
rows.Finding quote: Moreover, the levels of p62, which is associated with the degradation steps during autophagy, decreased following amino acid starvation more rapidly in APOE3 microglia compared to APOE4 microglia (0.592 ± 0.012 and 0.592 ± 0.011 compared to 0.932 ± 0.065, and 0.889 ± 0.053, respectively).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less p62 reduction after 0.5 h starvation)
rows.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; 0.5 h EBSS starvation; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to each line's time-zero control. p62 abundance is used as a degradation surrogate; lipid metabolism was not measured.
rows.Data location: Fig. 3, p62 densitometry among panels B–D; individual letter unspecified

rows.Finding description: After 100 nM rapamycin, normalized p62 was higher in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia: 1.055 ± 0.055 versus 0.777 ± 0.063, indicating less p62 reduction.
rows.Finding quote: Accordingly, the LC3II/actin ratio under these conditions was 1.508 ± 0.043 and 1.522 ± 0.069 in APOE3 expressing microglia, compared to 1.171 ± 0.078 and 1.33 ± 0.112, in APOE4 expressing microglia, (Fig. 4) whereas the corresponding p62 levels were 0.777 ± 0.063 and 0.706 ± 0.079, compared to 1.055 ± 0.055 and 1.026 ± 0.063, in APOE4 expressing microglia, which did not show any change in p62 levels during the experimental time frame (Fig. 4).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less p62 reduction with 100 nM rapamycin)
rows.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 24 h; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to each line's untreated control. p62 abundance is an autophagic-degradation surrogate; lipid mediation was not tested.

rows.Finding description: Starvation-induced LC3 and p62 changes in APOE4 microglia were interpreted as weaker autophagy induction than in APOE3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Thus, the results suggest that induction of autophagy may be also impaired in APOE4 microglia.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (weaker starvation-induced autophagy-marker responses)
rows.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4; amino-acid starvation in EBSS; LC3-I, LC3-II and p62 measured by western blot. No lipid-metabolism measurements or human-derived cells.

rows.Finding description: Following Aβ washout, APOE4 microglia showed less fluorescent Aβ loss, interpreted as lower Aβ degradation, than APOE3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Next, we measured the rate of Aβ degradation in APOE3 compared to APOE4 cells, and as shown the degradation of Aβ was significantly higher in APOE3 expressing cells compared to APOE4 expressing microglial cells (Fig. 2B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower apparent intracellular Aβ degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4; loaded with 0.1 µM HiLyte 488-Aβ1–42 for 2 h, washed twice with PBS, then imaged for 2 h in Aβ-free medium; intracellular fluorescence loss used as degradation readout. Lysosomal specificity and lipid mediation were not established.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Across three experiments with 7–10 images per line per experiment, APOE4 iAstrocytes showed greater cholesterol colocalization with dextran-labeled lysosomes than APOE3, with E4–E3 statistical significance unspecified.
rows.Finding quote: Further colocalization of Filipin III with Dextran-Alexa 555 was highest in APOE4 iAstrocytes, indicating higher cholesterol levels in lysosomes of APOE4 iAstrocytes (E4 > E2) (Figure 3G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater cholesterol localization in iAstrocyte lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline. Cells received 0.2 mg/mL Dextran-Alexa 555 overnight followed by a 14-hour chase, 10 mM methyl-β-cyclodextrin for 30 minutes, fixation, and Filipin III staining for two hours. Confocal colocalization was normalized to APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, the lysosomal activity assay showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 iAstrocytes, although both had lower activity than APOE2 and APOE-KO cells.
rows.Finding quote: Lysosomal activity in APOE3 and APOE4 was significantly lower than in APOE2 and APOE-KO cells (KO = E2 > E3 = E4) (Figure 4F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal activity in iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; lysosomal activity assay normalized to APOE3. The assay reagent, substrate, and assay duration are not specified in the supplied text.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, LAMP2 immunofluorescence showed no significant difference in lysosome-covered cell area between APOE4 and APOE3 iAstrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Immunofluorescent detection of lysosomes by LAMP2 (Figure 4C) or Dextran-Alexa 555 (Figure S3) showed no difference between genotypes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LAMP2-positive lysosomal area in iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; LAMP2 immunocytochemistry with GFAP costaining, quantified as percentage of cell area. Compartment area provides a structural surrogate for lysosomal status.

rows.Finding description: Western blots from three independent experiments showed significantly lower LAMP2 protein abundance in APOE4 than APOE3 iAstrocytes, providing a lysosomal-marker readout.
rows.Finding quote: However, protein levels of LAMP2 detected by western blot were significantly higher in APOE3 compared with APOE2, APOE4, and APOE-KO (E3 > E2 = E4 = KO) (Figures 4D and 4E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LAMP2 protein abundance in iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; lysate western blots for LAMP2 and RAB5. This record concerns LAMP2; its quantification is presented in Fig 4E.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Representative immunocytochemistry images showed decreased LAMP1-positive lysosome staining in APOE4 versus APOE3 astrocytes, from experiments comprising 18 wells per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Compared to APOE3 astrocytes, APOE4 astrocytes showed decreased levels of all three downstream endosomal compartment markers (RAB11, RAB7, LAMP1) indicating dysfunction throughout the endocytic pathway.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (decreased LAMP1-positive lysosome staining in human astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173 isogenic homozygous APOE3/APOE4 line pairs; four-day serum withdrawal before fixation and LAMP1 immunocytochemistry; representative confocal images.

rows.Finding description: Increasing INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes produced no significant difference in RAB7-positive late endosome staining compared with the darkGFP expression control.
rows.Finding quote: Increasing either PICALM or INPP5D expression had no detectable effect on either RAB11-positive recycling endosomes (Figure 5E, 5F) or RAB7-positive late endosomes (Figure 5G, 5H).
rows.Finding summary: (increased INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (no change in RAB7-positive late endosome staining)
rows.Experimental system: Human homozygous APOE4 iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173; lentiviral INPP5D expression versus lentiviral darkGFP control, followed by serum withdrawal; fixed-cell RAB7 immunocytochemistry and confocal image quantification.

rows.Finding description: Increasing INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes reduced LAMP1-positive lysosome staining compared with darkGFP control, without establishing whether lysosomal function improved or worsened.
rows.Finding quote: Increased INPP5D expression did result in reduced LAMP1-positive lysosome staining compared to darkGFP (Figure 5I, 5J).
rows.Finding summary: (increased INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (decreased LAMP1-positive lysosome staining)
rows.Experimental system: Human homozygous APOE4 iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173; lentiviral INPP5D expression versus lentiviral darkGFP control, followed by serum withdrawal; fixed-cell LAMP1 immunocytochemistry and confocal image quantification.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Rapamycin induced autophagy-associated fluorescence in human ApoE3-expressing T98G cells but failed to induce it in ApoE4-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: Rapamycin induced autophagy in T98G-E3 cells; however, it did not induce autophagy in T98G-E4 cells (Fig. 4g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower rapamycin-induced autophagy-associated fluorescence)
rows.Experimental system: Human glioblastoma T98G stable transformants expressing ApoE3 or ApoE4; 1 µM rapamycin; Abcam ab139484 autophagy-detection staining and fluorescence microscopy. The associated quantification reports three biological repeats, each with 15–20 images per group. This staining does not independently establish autophagic flux, and lipid metabolism was not measured.

rows.Finding description: Quantified autophagy-associated fluorescence was lower in ApoE4-expressing than ApoE3-expressing human T98G cells under the reported autophagy-induction conditions.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, measurement of autophagy in live cells showed that active autophagy levels were low in T98G-E4 cells compared to T98G-E3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagy-associated fluorescence)
rows.Experimental system: Human glioblastoma T98G stable transformants expressing ApoE3 or ApoE4; fluorescence quantification per cell following Abcam ab139484 staining in the rapamycin/CBA2 experiment; three biological repeats with 15–20 images per group per experiment. Neither lipid metabolism nor lysosomal degradation flux was directly measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Isogenic human APOE4 astrocytes had lower SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 levels than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with impaired lysosomal cholesterol export.
rows.Finding quote: Negatively enriched Lysosome (Figures 2F and S3D) and lower SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 in APOE4 vs. APOE3 astrocytes (Figure S6D) indicates cholesterol transport out of lysosomes may be impaired by APOE4.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower astrocyte SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 levels)
rows.Experimental system: Human hiPSC-derived isogenic APOE4 and APOE3 astrocytes in the cholesterol-trafficking experiments using Indiv1 and Indiv2, which share local haplotype hap.03. The available text identifies the measured regulators but does not specify this supplementary panel's assay, treatment duration or n.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Quantification in 12 mice per genotype assessed BODIPY-positive lipids within CD68-positive lysosomes, with the text reporting large microglial phagolysosomal accumulations in TE4 mice and no substantial glial lipid staining in TE3 mice.
rows.Finding quote: Importantly, while we did not detect substantial levels of neutral or oxidized lipids in glia of TEKO or TE3 mice by immunostaining, large accumulations of BODIPY+ neutral lipids were observed within microglial phagolysosomes of TE4 mice.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, with P301S tauopathy) -> (increased phagolysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation; impaired degradation inferred)
rows.Experimental system: Hippocampal microglia in 9.5-month-old human APOE3- or APOE4-expressing PS19 P301S tau mice, murine Apoe-null background; C57BL/6-backcrossed P301S line; 6 male and 6 female mice per genotype; BODIPY/Iba1/CD68 staining and IMARIS compartmental colocalization analysis. No lysosomal degradation-rate, pH, or enzyme-activity assay was reported.
rows.Data location: Fig. 2C; TE4-versus-TE3 contrast also explicitly described in the Discussion sentence beginning 'Importantly, while we did not detect substantial levels'

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: Adding apoE4 caused a small increase in internalized ApoER2 relative to untreated controls in mouse N2a-APPsw cells.
rows.Finding quote: We observed small increases of ApoER2 and β-secretase in response to ApoE and ApoE4 ( Fig. 2 c ), whereas the increase of APP was much greater, ∼2.5 and fourfold in response to ApoE and ApoE4, respectively ( Fig. 2 c ).
rows.Finding summary: (no added apoE4 -> added apoE4) -> (more internalized ApoER2)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human Swedish-mutant APP, supplied by Dr. Riqiang Yan, transiently transfected with murine ApoER2 and human β-secretase. Surface proteins were pulse-labeled with cleavable sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin at 4°C, then allowed to internalize for 15 min at 37°C in control medium or medium containing 10 μg/ml apoE4. Surface biotin was stripped with glutathione; protected intracellular biotinylated proteins were recovered with NeutrAvidin agarose and analyzed by Western blot. This was not a human brain-cell system.
